episode_title: Is Your AI Pilot Too Snazzy to Survive Production?

real_qa.q: What foundational elements should organizations implement before moving AI pilots into production?
real_qa.r: Organizations must start with defining upfront what the agent is allowed to do, what data it has access to, how that data is governed, who has access to it, and ensure that any action of consequence from the agent is logged in an auditable way. Everything the agent takes in, all decisions it makes, what resources it accesses when it passes off to a human—all must be in an auditable log with processes in place to review that evidence and make determinations whether the agent is performing as intended.
real_qa.requete: AI agent production governance logging framework

real_qa.q: How should organizations balance encouraging AI experimentation with preventing shadow AI and uncontrolled agent tasks?
real_qa.r: Organizations need to encourage innovation and agency while avoiding a mountain of technical debt. The bottoms-up approach grants power to users who previously relied on IT, but without correct permissions setup, an agentic task could impact hundreds or thousands of records without the right governance. The solution is distributing AI through targeted applications within business processes—like when a loan application is submitted or prescription is granted—with structured processes, evaluation, and audit in place.
real_qa.requete: shadow AI governance enterprise risk management

real_qa.q: How is Salesforce's shift toward headless architecture changing its strategic positioning beyond CRM?
real_qa.r: Salesforce is positioning itself as a platform as a service where CRM is just one app built on that platform. With headless architecture, companies can make customer or partner experiences wholly their own, rebrand them close to their business as the fabric of interactions, keep parts in their own stack, and have interaction with Salesforce be skinnier. This natural extension reflects how Salesforce is moving beyond traditional CRM into a broader platform strategy.
real_qa.requete: Salesforce headless architecture CRM platform strategy

real_qa.q: What consumption-based licensing changes might Salesforce implement to help organizations shift to newer products?
real_qa.r: Salesforce is expected to continue driving toward consumption-based models instead of seat-based licensing, which could create more flexibility. This would allow customers who have parts of the platform they are not utilizing as much to shift focus and adopt newer technologies and features without being locked into static licensing arrangements.

real_qa.q: How should organizations measure ROI and performance when implementing AI agents within business processes?
real_qa.r: Organizations should have mature processes around logging evidence and creating a chain of evidence for review. They need concrete mechanisms for calculating ROI of the process and evaluating agent performance with clear metrics. This evidence-based framework allows organizations to determine whether an agent should earn more authority or have authority dialed back based on actual performance data.
real_qa.requete: AI agent ROI measurement performance evaluation metrics
